name: Liberal feminism
summary: Liberal feminism seeks equality between women and men through legal and political reform within liberal democracy, treating the denial of equal rights, education and economic opportunity as the main barrier. It works through legislatures, courts and enforcement of anti-discrimination law, aims to integrate women into the mainstream of public life, and welcomes men as partners. Its economics range from center-right to center-left.
scope: The mainstream liberal feminist tradition from Wollstonecraft and John Stuart Mill's Subjection of Women to the 1966 NOW Statement of Purpose (Friedan, Murray) and modern liberal feminist political philosophy (Okin, Nussbaum). It excludes radical, socialist and Marxist feminism, and libertarian and neoliberal variants are treated as strands. Many non-gender statements are inferred from center-left liberal democracy and given low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Betty Friedan

sources.author: NOW (Friedan and Murray)
sources.usedFor: Program of enforcing equal rights, childcare and retraining, equal education, and partnership with men.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a defining issue, but NOW-style liberal feminism backs public provision of services such as childcare and reproductive care and sits center-left on material inequality.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Women are over-represented in low-paid work, and the NOW statement cites the pay gap, so mainstream liberal feminists generally back wage floors; the sources do not name a figure.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Liberal feminism spans center-right to center-left on economics, so adherents are split; the mainstream treats the state as a needed enforcer of equal treatment rather than trusting markets alone.

public-ownership.rationale: Liberal feminism works within existing capitalist liberal democracy and does not call for public ownership of industry; this is left to socialist feminists.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Social-democratic strands support measures to reduce material inequality, though the neoliberal strand does not; the mainstream leans mildly in favour.

unions-good.rationale: NOW's statement calls for opening unions to women and challenging discrimination within them, treating unions as institutions to integrate rather than reject, and the mainstream is union-friendly.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mill and early liberal feminists prized married women's property rights, but the sources give no view on property as a near-absolute right.

cut-welfare.rationale: NOW opposes policies that foster dependence yet wants childcare and retraining programs; adherents do not generally favour cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership belongs to socialist feminism; liberal feminism seeks integration into the existing economy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No stated position; the individual-autonomy emphasis pulls toward yes while the center-left mainstream is cautious, so adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Liberal feminists are divided between free-speech liberalism and anti-discrimination protections; the sources state no common position.

strong-leader.rationale: Liberal feminism pursues reform through law, legislatures and rights within liberal democracy, which is at odds with leaders bypassing constraints.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberal feminism relies on the state and law to end discrimination and is associated with state feminism; the NOW statement demands federal enforcement.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Liberal feminists are divided: autonomy arguments favour legalisation, while NOW generally opposes prostitution though divided on how to approach it.

decide-locally.rationale: NOW seeks national enforcement of equal rights through the Constitution and federal law, so adherents lean towards national standards over local discretion.

traditional-family.rationale: NOW wants new institutions so that women need not be defined by child-rearing, and Mill attacks the legal authority of the husband; adherents reject the traditional family as society's foundation without disparaging family life.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Liberal feminism treats LGBT rights as a core issue in the 21st century and extends equal civil rights to all.

abortion-legal.rationale: Freer access to abortion is a listed priority of NOW and liberal feminism, framed through privacy and women's autonomy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not a stated aim; liberal feminism's secular rights framework and history of challenging churches as discriminating institutions point to a mild no.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Liberal feminists back affirmative action and take an intersectional approach today; NOW's statement stresses that human rights are indivisible.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Mill argued that what is called women's nature is an eminently artificial thing shaped by circumstances, which liberal feminism inherits; adherents stop short of denying all innate difference.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not a feminist concern; liberal feminists generally put universal individual rights ahead of custom, which Mill calls weak evidence of merit.

gradual-change.rationale: Liberal feminism favours gradual reform through institutions over revolution.

revolution-justified.rationale: Liberal feminism favours gradual reform within liberal democracy, in contrast to radical and socialist feminists.

central-planning.rationale: Liberal feminism accepts existing market economies and gives no support to planning, which Marxist feminists rather than liberal ones advance.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Mill's liberalism accepted limited inheritance taxation, but adherents have no common position.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing wage labor is a Marxist feminist demand; liberal feminism seeks women's equal access to paid work.

one-party-rule.rationale: Liberal feminism operates within liberal democracy and pluralist political participation.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to dynastic-succession: its rationale is about inherited rule, and this statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state.

reviewHistory.rationale: Mill attacks inherited, unchosen authority; adherents are mildly opposed though constitutional monarchy is not at issue.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to dynastic-succession: its rationale is about inherited rule, and this statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

democracy-best.rationale: Winning equal political rights and a place in the decision-making mainstream is central, and suffrage is a founding aim.

workers-councils.rationale: A socialist institution that liberal feminism does not advance; it works through parliaments and courts.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mill argued that male authority came from force and custom, and that natural fitness cannot be known when circumstances restrict women; liberal feminism rejects ascribed fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not directly addressed; reformist and pro-legal change means adherents mostly reject violence, though not absolutely.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Liberal feminism grounds rights in equal individual autonomy, not scripture, and challenges religious justifications of women's subordination.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Liberal feminism depends on public enforcement of equal rights, which libertarian privatisation would remove.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Universal human rights and the indivisibility of rights, as NOW states, are at odds with an ethnically defined nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Marxist reading of class conflict is rejected; liberal feminism seeks equality within existing society and welcomes cross-class coalitions.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Liberal feminism focuses on equality of opportunity and removal of legal barriers, though some strands support measures against material inequality.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Liberal feminism is individualistic, yet neoliberal and social-democratic strands differ and the sources do not endorse self-interest as a moral doctrine.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Liberal feminism is a rights-based doctrine in which equal individual rights come first.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy appears nowhere in the liberal feminist sources, and adherents divide between privacy and safety arguments.

restore-past-order.rationale: Liberal feminism aims to overturn historical legal subordination of women and does not prize a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No stated position; the pragmatic style of liberal feminism pulls yes while principled rights claims pull no.

direct-action.rationale: Liberal feminism works through law, lobbying and elections more than direct action, which radical feminists favour.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Liberal feminists want sexual division of labor removed by choice, not abolition of the division of labor in general.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mill and NOW stress opportunity and equal pay for work, not distribution by need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist theory of exploitation belongs to socialist feminism, which liberal feminism is contrasted with.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with liberal democracy and gradual reform.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist claim not held by liberal feminism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Liberal feminism asks for state action and funded programmes such as childcare; the libertarian claim is rejected by mainstream adherents.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill, the harm principle's author, is a founding liberal feminist; adherents back it broadly while some accept limits on harmful speech or exploitation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberal feminism is individualistic and treats women as individuals with rights, though group-based anti-discrimination law is accepted.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Political voice and the vote are central to the liberal feminist programme.

positive-liberty.rationale: Liberal feminism backs childcare, retraining and equal-opportunity enforcement so women can act on their freedom, and social-democratic strands support material measures.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Liberal feminism rejects ascribed group inferiority and takes an intersectional, anti-discrimination stance.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Mill and other liberal feminists rejected rule founded on personal authority rather than law and consent.

bound-labor.rationale: Mill compares women's subjection to slavery and demands freedom of occupation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mill's emphasis on custom as untested bias gives it some purchase, yet liberal feminism relies on shared reason and evidence, unlike standpoint theory.

universal-morality.rationale: Liberal feminism rests on universal moral claims about equal worth and human rights, though critics say the universals were particulars.

single-common-good.rationale: Liberal pluralism accepts competing interests and women's claims as one of them.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarian and neoliberal strands agree, social-democratic ones do not.

rule-by-example.rationale: Liberal feminism wants legal rights and enforcement, not reliance on rulers' virtue; Mill attacks reliance on unchecked power.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Wollstonecraft and Mill grounded women's equality in reason and denied that custom or sentiment justifies subordination, though modern adherents include religious women.

class-collaboration.rationale: Liberal feminism pursues pragmatic cross-class coalitions and partnership with men rather than opposed camps.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts are not part of liberal feminism's concerns, and its universalist stance pulls against it, leaving no clear adherent view.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Mill argues that occupations should be open to all capable people regardless of sex, and NOW demands equal partnership.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The NOW statement states human rights are indivisible and links women's cause to civil rights.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Liberal feminism treats the state as a tool women can use to secure equality, unlike the Marxist view.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in the sources and contrary to egalitarian liberalism.

national-mission.rationale: A national mission to spread a form of government is not a liberal feminist theme, and adherents are divided between rights promotion and scepticism of it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Liberal feminists hold that law and custom have systematically disadvantaged women and call for deliberate legal correction, as Mill and the NOW Statement of Purpose document.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale infers the answer from the subject being or backing the establishment, not from a stated view of how politicians behave.

reviewHistory.rationale: Liberal feminism seeks to enter existing political institutions, not denounce them wholesale.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale infers the answer from the subject being or backing the establishment, not from a stated view of how politicians behave.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts the liberal feminist commitment to reproductive autonomy and equal moral worth.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Liberal feminism calls for federal enforcement, childcare centres and retraining, which exceed a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts equal rights and indivisible human rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The NOW statement begins with women as human beings entitled to full development, and liberal feminism rests on equal respect for persons.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal legal status for women across personal-law systems is a liberal feminist goal, as Mill demanded one legal standard for marriage.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Liberal feminism grounds legitimate government in equal participation and consent, and fought for women's inclusion in that consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts the rights framework and equal human rights.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The libertarian absolute is not held by mainstream liberal feminism, though libertarian feminists do hold it.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine contrary to liberal pluralism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Intersectional, inclusive liberal feminism rejects this.

party-controls-media.rationale: Incompatible with liberal democracy and free expression.

clerical-rule.rationale: Contradicts secular rights liberalism and women's equality.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist slogan alien to liberal feminism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Mill's liberalism opposes moral censorship; liberal feminism inherits this.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is outside liberal feminism's documented concerns, so no adherent position can be stated.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Liberal feminism prizes women's education, as NOW demands equal educational opportunity.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Liberal feminists criticise practices that subordinate women yet respect pluralism; critics of liberal feminism target its universalism, so adherents split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Education on sexuality and gender equality is a liberal feminist priority tied to reproductive autonomy and equal opportunity in schooling.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Liberal feminists lean against restriction on speech grounds, but NOW-linked feminists and others have supported limits, so adherents are divided.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Liberal feminists worry that exemptions let religious institutions discriminate against women, as NOW targets discrimination in churches.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's On Liberty argument for eccentricity underlies his case against custom, and he attacks social pressure shaping women.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Mill rejects authority resting on custom and unchosen status, and liberal democracy treats rulers as accountable.

character-from-environment.rationale: Wollstonecraft's and Mill's argument is that women's supposed nature is largely produced by education and circumstance.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is not part of liberal feminism's documented concerns, and adherents are indifferent or divided.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Liberal feminism relies on rule of law applied equally.

equal-parenting.rationale: Liberal feminists support shared parenting in principle but disagree about default presumptions in custody courts.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine foreign to the tradition.

women-must-cover.rationale: Liberal feminism defends women's autonomy to choose how to live and dress, rejecting legal compulsion.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not part of the documented programme, and liberal feminists are wary of group claims that constrain women yet also pluralist, leaving them split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist claim; liberal feminism emphasises law and ideas of equal rights.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal feminism depends on courts enforcing equal rights against majority prejudice, as the NOW statement demands.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Bringing women into the decision-making mainstream is a NOW aim, and liberal feminists tend to favour measures to secure equal representation, though some prefer merit-only access.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Contrary to gradual reform within liberal democracy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mill compares the subjection of women to birth-based exclusion and argues that no one should be barred by birth.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Liberal feminists back affirmative action, though some critics within it prefer class-based measures.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Liberal feminism works within capitalism and assumes reform can succeed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not held by liberal feminism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Liberal feminism demands laws against discriminatory practices, as the NOW statement does by pressing enforcement of Title VII.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: NOW demands enforcement of constitutional guarantees, and liberal feminists look to entrenched rights and courts to secure equality.

elective-rulers.rationale: Elective, accountable government with women's full participation is the liberal feminist standard.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Liberal feminism rejects paternalistic protection that fosters dependence, which NOW explicitly opposes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Liberal feminism is a participatory movement aiming at full public and political life.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: NOW protests false images of women in the media but liberal feminism does not accept the Frankfurt School thesis of pacification.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim; liberal feminism does not frame society as ruling-class hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim not held by liberal feminism.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations among communist parties are not a liberal feminist topic, so no adherent position can be stated.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: NOW says men are harmed by half-equality and seeks partnership with men, but liberal feminism does not make men's disadvantage a programme.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Mainstream liberal feminism treats violence against women as the central concern, though it does not deny men's victimisation.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberal feminism holds universal equal rights apply everywhere, though critics call this universalism a particular.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Contrary to civilian liberal democratic government.

paid-care-work.rationale: Liberal feminists want childcare and recognition of care, as NOW and Nussbaum stress, but wages-for-housework is a socialist feminist demand.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Mill demanded that the wife not be bound to bondage-like marriage and Stanton's work included divorce law reform.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not a theme of the sources; neoliberal strands tolerate it while social-democratic ones criticise it, so adherents split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Liberal feminism applies Mill's anti-subjection logic to rule by one group over another, and the NOW statement treats human rights as indivisible.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Liberal feminism works through law and the courts, so it accepts a general duty to obey while reforming it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A liberal movement committed to equal rights rejects conspiracy claims against minorities.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The NOW Statement of Purpose seeks equal partnership in marriage, not its abolition.

informal-organisation.rationale: It works through legislatures, courts and a formal organisation such as NOW.

religious-nation.rationale: Liberal feminism is secular-liberal and defines citizenship by equal rights, not religion.

defeat-communism.rationale: Liberal feminism has no distinct view on communism; adherents are split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Liberal feminism holds equality can be won through legal and political reform within the existing system, not by transforming it.

socialized-care.rationale: NOW proposed child-care centres and support so women can work, but not socialising all housework and childcare.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Liberal feminism works through legislatures, courts and open political participation within liberal democracy, so suppressing opposition contradicts its method.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Liberal feminism sits within liberal democracy's freedom of conscience and expression, and Mill argued against custom and authority as grounds for restraint.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Liberal feminism stresses equal access to representative institutions and public life more than direct participation, though it welcomes wider involvement; adherents are not clearly committed either way.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Liberal feminism targets legal and institutional sex discrimination as a separable barrier, and intersectional critiques are usually made against it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not a feminist issue and liberal feminists are split between autonomy arguments and concerns about pressure on vulnerable people.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation is a Marxist concept, and the scope excludes Marxist and socialist feminism; liberal feminists seek equal access to paid work rather than a critique of wage labour.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Liberal feminism rests on liberal democracy and equal citizenship, in which authority comes from consent, and Mill attacked custom and inherited authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Liberal feminists split between neutrality of the state and individual freedom and women's autonomy in choosing dress; the sources do not settle it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Liberal feminism centres on enforcing anti-discrimination law through the courts, which the NOW program stresses, so keeping harassment claims out of court runs against its method.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Mill attacks inherited, unchosen authority; adherents are mildly opposed though constitutional monarchy is not at issue. (Moved from monarchy-legitimate, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about ceremonial heads of state.)

property-franchise.rationale: Its core claim is equal political rights regardless of sex, resting on universal citizenship rather than a wealth test.

racial-franchise.rationale: The NOW Statement of Purpose demands equality and opposes discrimination and denial of rights on grounds of race as well as sex.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Mill demanded legal equality and freedom within marriage, which rules out state limits on whom adults may marry.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: NOW rejected discrimination and exclusion as contrary to equal rights and full participation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not a defining issue; liberal feminism is generally center-left on material inequality and worried about concentrated economic power, though market-liberal strands differ.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Liberal feminism assumes liberal neutrality and freedom of conscience, so state promotion of atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: It works through law enforcement and the courts to secure rights, so abolishing police and prisons runs against its method.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Its equality principle favours women's eligibility for all offices, though liberal feminism respects religious freedom and so does not seek to compel it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Mill's Subjection of Women attacks the husband's legal authority and the NOW Statement of Purpose calls for a truly equal partnership in marriage.

rent-control.rationale: Liberal feminism is split between market-oriented and welfare-oriented strands on housing regulation; it has no stated position.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Liberal feminism's economic views range from centre-right to centre-left; it is not clearly for or against this.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Liberal feminism generally distinguishes biological sex from socially constructed gender, treating the sex-gender distinction as standard.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Liberal feminism organises around women as a shared group in seeking equal rights, so it does not reject the category.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Liberal feminism is indifferent to the territorial organisation of peoples.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Liberal feminism works within liberal democracy and excludes Marxist and socialist feminism, so it does not make working-class rule the test of socialism.

municipal-property.rationale: Liberal feminism accepts private property and markets within liberal democracy, and does not call for community ownership.

family-wage.rationale: NOW and Mill reject treating women as dependants and press equal pay, so a wage set to support a worker's family assumes a male breadwinner model they oppose.

person-over-state.rationale: Mill's individual liberty and equal rights for each person are core liberal feminist claims, as is each woman as an end in herself.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Liberal feminism is secular in method and neutral about spirituality; adherents differ.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Liberal feminism stresses women's equal rationality and the same rights as men, in contrast to difference or care feminism, so it resists giving women's presumed distinct values extra weight.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Liberal feminism works through legislatures, courts and enforcement of existing law to integrate women into the mainstream (s1, s4), so smashing the state is rejected.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Liberal feminism grounds rights in shared human capacities for autonomy and equal respect (s2) and Mill rejected custom as proof of a different nature for women (s3); 'should not be redesigned' goes beyond the sources, so medium.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Mill and the NOW statement demand equal legal rights for women in property and marriage, which covers owning and inheriting land.

premarital-sex.rationale: The NOW Statement of Purpose backs women's control over their sexual and reproductive lives and rejects the sexual double standard.

women-suffrage.rationale: Votes for women and equal political rights are the founding demand of the liberal feminist tradition, argued in Mill's Subjection of Women and the NOW Statement.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Liberal feminists are split: some criticise patriarchal religious norms (Okin) while many are religious and see faith as compatible with equality.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Liberal feminism does not address how unowned land is first owned, and its strands range from libertarian to social-liberal, so this is split.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Equal partnership and equal rights for women follow directly from the NOW statement's program, so group self-rule should not be exempt from them.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Strands differ, from left-libertarian egalitarian views to market-liberal ones; no mainstream position.

self-ownership.rationale: Mill and the NOW Statement stress women's right to control their own persons, labour and reproductive lives.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The tradition works through legislatures, courts and parties to win equal rights, not around them.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Mill and the NOW Statement call for equal rights in marriage law, which includes equal ability to end a marriage.

material-over-identity.rationale: Liberal feminism's agenda is equal rights and opportunity for women, which includes the identity issues this statement tells the left to put aside.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Liberal feminism works within liberal democracy and rejects communist party rule.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: NOW opposes policies that foster dependence yet wants childcare and retraining programs; adherents do not generally favour cutting welfare. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: The law should require equal pay for equal work regardless of sex.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1966 NOW statement documents the pay gap and presses enforcement of Title VII against sex discrimination in employment.

missingStatements.text: Governments should fund public childcare so that parents can stay in paid work.
missingStatements.rationale: NOW proposed a nationwide network of child-care centres and retraining so women need not leave public life.
missingStatements.declined: Public childcare funding is a policy detail; paid-care-work is not the same question and this view is single-audit.

missingStatements.text: Married women should have the same legal rights to property, earnings and children as their husbands.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill criticised the wife's near-bondage in law, with her property and earnings passing to the husband, and demanded legal equality.

notes: Strands differ on markets (neoliberal and libertarian vs social-democratic), sex work and pornography, and abortion within some groups. Most non-gender answers are low-confidence inferences.
